bom.function: Right-angle SMD tactile button (Würth). Side-mounted page navigation buttons (left and right of the device body).
Right-angle SMD slide switch (C&K, SPDT). Power on/off slide switch on the device side.
Dual AAA battery holder (Keystone). SMD-mounted; the 1022C retainer clip is required separately to keep cells in place.
P-channel MOSFET. Q1 (gate = EN / GPIO18) switches the +3.3VP rail powering the SD card and flash chip. Q2 (gate = ~EN2 / GPIO15) switches the C2 module's 3.3 V supply.
10 µF MLCC, 1206, ≥6.3 V. Bulk decoupling on the battery rail (+BATT) and the switched 3.3 V rail (+3.3VP).
1 µF MLCC, 0805, ≥6.3 V. Local decoupling on the 3V3 rail.
10 kΩ, 1206. Pull-ups on the shared SPI bus (SCK and MISO lines) for the flash chip (U4).
The MCU. Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040 @ 133 MHz, 264 KB SRAM, 2 MB onboard flash). Runs the libros firmware. SC0918 and SC0915 are two RPi distributor SKUs for the same Pico board.
Push/push microSD card slot. Holds the book library on a microSD card — UTF-8 .txt files with support for bold, italic, chapter breaks, and front-matter metadata via inline control codes.
16 Mb SPI NOR flash. Stores the GNU Unifont + per-language glyph data that doesn't fit in the Pico's 2 MB flash. Read over the shared SPI bus via /BABEL_CS.

3 × 6 mm through-hole tactile button (E-Switch). The menu / directional / select cluster under the screen. 7 placements (B3–B9). The BOM specifies the 180WQ (1.8 N, firmer click); the upstream README links to the 130WQ (1.3 N, lighter touch). Either fits the same footprint — order whichever feel you prefer.
3-pin JST PH SMD connector (STEMMA). OPTIONAL expansion port: power + I²C / GPIO for add-ons (reading light, accessibility input).
4-pin JST SH SMD connector (STEMMA QT). OPTIONAL dedicated I²C expansion port.
1 kΩ, 0805. OPTIONAL pull-ups — install only if the STEMMA / I²C expansion ports are used.

bom.description: Oddly Specific castellated E-paper driver module
bom.function: Castellated e-paper driver submodule. Generates the ±22 V and ±15 V rails the e-paper panel needs, converts signal levels between the Pico and the display, and drives the FFC ribbon. Ordered pre-assembled from JLCPCB or PCBWay; soldered to the C1 main board via castellated edge pads.

4.2-inch B&W e-paper panel (GoodDisplay), 400 × 300 px, SPI interface, connects via FFC to the C2 driver module. The BOM lists the GDEW042T2 but you'll receive a GDEY042T81 — same connector, drop-in compatible. Order the B&W variant specifically.
0.47 Ω sense resistor, 0603. Current-sense feedback for the boost converter that generates the e-paper high-voltage rails.
10 µH inductor, 0805, 500 mA. Energy storage for the boost converter.

bom.description: 1uF ±10% 50V X7R 0805 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors MLCC - SMD/SMT RoHS
bom.function: 1 µF MLCC, 0805, 50 V, X7R. Bypass and filter capacitors throughout the driver circuit (9 placements).

bom.description: 4.7uF ±10% 25V X5R 0805 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors MLCC - SMD/SMT RoHS
bom.function: 4.7 µF MLCC, 0805, 25 V, X5R. Bulk decoupling on the driver power rails.

bom.description: Contact,Top 24 0.020"（0.50mm） 0.079"（2.00mm） Slide Lock 24P FFC, FPC Connectors RoHS
bom.function: 24-pin 0.5 mm FFC connector. Connects the flat flex cable from the e-paper display panel.
N-channel MOSFET, 100 V, 1.6 A, SOT-23. Switches the e-paper gate driver voltage rail.
30 V Schottky diode, SOD-123. Charge-pump rectifiers for the negative voltage rails (3 placements).

assembly.title: Order the C1 main board (bare PCB) and the C2 e-paper driver (pre-assembled board)
assembly.description: Before you solder anything, get both boards fabricated. The C1 main board ships as a bare PCB; the C2 castellated (half-circle edge pads) e-paper driver arrives pre-assembled. See the ordering guide on the About tab for exact gerber files and PCB specs (1.0 mm thickness, lead-free HASL).
assembly.notes: Upload OSO-BOOK-C1-05-rounded.zip to your PCB fab for C1. For the C2 driver: use OSO-BOOK-C2-02 files for PCBWay assembly (PCBA) or OSO-BOOK-C2-03 for JLCPCB PCBA.

assembly.title: Solder surface-mount (SMD) passives on C1: 10 µF, 1 µF, 10 kΩ (and optionally 1 kΩ)
assembly.description: Start with the smallest surface-mount passives. C1 and C2 are 10 µF 1206 caps. C3 is a 1 µF 0805 cap. R3 and R4 are 10 kΩ 1206 resistors. If you want the STEMMA expansion, also install R1 and R2 (1 kΩ 0805). These take flux and a fine tip but don't require hot air.
assembly.notes: R1/R2 are OPTIONAL — install them if you plan to use the STEMMA/I²C expansion ports.

assembly.title: Solder surface-mount chips on C1: flash chip and MOSFETs
assembly.description: U4 is the GD25Q16C 16 Mb flash chip (SOIC-8, an 8-pin chip package). Q1 and Q2 are P-channel DMG3415U-7 MOSFETs (SOT-23, a 3-pin chip package). Use flux and drag-solder technique (run the iron tip slowly across all pins at once) for U4; Q1/Q2 are 3-pin, easy one-pin-at-a-time.
assembly.notes: Watch Q1/Q2 orientation — the DMG3415U-7 is P-channel.

assembly.title: Solder surface-mount connectors and switches on C1: µSD slot, side buttons, slide switch
assembly.description: U3 is the GCT MEM2075 microSD push/push slot (fine-pitch metal shell — solder the shell tabs first for alignment). B1 and B2 are Würth right-angle tactile buttons. SW1 is the C&K power slide switch. Install the optional J1/J2/J3 JST connectors in this step too if you're using expansion.
assembly.notes: The SD slot has both signal pins and shell tabs — tack the shell tabs first to prevent the slot from shifting while you solder the signal pins.

assembly.title: Solder the Keystone 1022 battery holder + 1022C retainer clip on C1
assembly.description: BT1 is the dual-AAA battery holder (surface-mount through-pad). These pads draw heat — use a larger tip and extra flux. Install the 1022C retainer clip, which physically retains the AAA cells.
assembly.notes: The 1022C retainer clip is easy to miss — make sure you've ordered it (Digi-Key 36-1022C-ND).

assembly.title: Solder the C2 e-paper driver module onto C1 via castellated edges (the row of half-circle pads along the board edge)
assembly.description: U2 is the pre-assembled Castellated E-Paper Driver. Drop it into its footprint on the main board and solder the castellated pads. The module generates the ±22 V and ±15 V rails the e-paper needs.
assembly.notes: The C2 internals were assembled at the fab house. Solder the castellated edge pads to the matching C1 pads beneath.

assembly.title: Solder the 7 through-hole tactile buttons on C1 (B3–B9)
assembly.description: The menu / directional / select cluster under the screen: 7× TL1107AF180WQ. Install from the front of the board; solder on the back. Push buttons face outwards (away from the PCB).
assembly.notes: These are gullwing-style — make sure the tactile switch body seats flat against the board before soldering. Note: the BOM specifies TL1107AF180WQ (1.8 N, firmer click) but the README links to 130WQ (1.3 N, lighter touch). Either fits the same footprint.

assembly.title: Solder the Raspberry Pi Pico (U1) onto C1
assembly.description: The Pico can be installed in two ways: through-hole pin headers (if you want it removable for reflashing) or reflowed via its castellated edge pads (flush, permanent). The castellated method gives the slimmest profile.
assembly.notes: Pin headers make reflashing easy if you plan to iterate on firmware. Castellated gives the slimmest profile for a finished device.

assembly.title: Attach the e-paper panel via FFC (flat ribbon cable) to the C2 module
assembly.description: Slide the panel's FPC (flexible printed circuit) tail into the 24-pin 0.5 mm FFC connector (the latching clip) on the C2 module. Make sure the contact side faces the correct way (check the connector's latching direction). Close the connector latch.
assembly.notes: Order a 4.2-inch B&W GoodDisplay panel — you'll receive a GDEY042T81. The firmware auto-detects it via PR #11. Order the B&W variant specifically.

assembly.title: Build and flash the libros firmware onto the Pico
assembly.description: Clone joeycastillo/libros from GitHub. The Pico build needs two community PRs from @tahnok: PR #10 (fixes a broken Pico build by removing a stray pico/stdlib.h include) and PR #11 (runtime e-ink driver selection so the firmware works with the newer GDEY042T81 display). Cherry-pick both, then build with the Pico SDK to produce a .uf2 file. To flash: hold BOOTSEL (the small button on the Pico board) while plugging it into USB — it appears as a USB drive. Drag-and-drop the .uf2 file onto it. The Pico reboots into libros.
assembly.notes: PR #10 (https://github.com/joeycastillo/libros/pull/10) and PR #11 (https://github.com/joeycastillo/libros/pull/11) are both unmerged but both required for a clean Pico build today. PR #11 auto-detects display controller via busy-pin polarity — works with the GDEY042T81 and the older GDEW042T2. A pre-built book.uf2 is available at https://oddlyspecificobjects.com/projects/openbook/ but only targets the GDEW042T2; for the GDEY042T81 you must build from source with both PRs applied.

assembly.title: Flash babel.bin (font/glyph data) to the SPI flash chip
assembly.description: On first boot after flashing libros, the firmware needs GNU Unifont bitmap data on the external GD25Q16C flash chip (U4) to render text. Download babel.bin from the project page and flash it to the SPI flash using the libros bootloader's built-in flash utility. This takes about a minute.
assembly.notes: babel.bin is available at https://oddlyspecificobjects.com/projects/openbook/. It contains GNU Unifont bitmap data covering the entire Unicode Basic Multilingual Plane — Latin, Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, and more, with automatic right-to-left text detection.

assembly.title: Prepare a microSD card with books
assembly.description: Format a microSD card as FAT (the standard SD card format — most cards ship this way). Copy UTF-8 .txt files onto it — first line of each file is the book title. The firmware supports bold, italic, chapter title pages, and front-matter metadata (title, author, description, genre, language) via inline control codes.
assembly.notes: Any capacity works — even 256 MB is enough for hundreds of books. Formatting reference: Shift In (U+000F) toggles italic → bold+italic, Shift Out (U+000E) reverts; Record Separator (U+001E) at the start of a line creates a chapter title page at 2× size. Front matter goes between --- delimiters with TITL/AUTH/DESC/GNRE/LANG keys. Full details at https://oddlyspecificobjects.com/projects/openbook/. The libros-convert tool (https://github.com/joeycastillo/libros-convert) converts Standard Ebooks EPUBs into this format automatically.

assembly.title: 3D-print the case and assemble
assembly.description: Print 'Open Book Abridged - Minimal Case.stl' from the upstream repo's 3D Printed Case directory (https://github.com/joeycastillo/The-Open-Book/tree/main/3D%20Printed%20Case). The STL prints support-free on any FDM printer. Fit the completed board, insert 2× AAA batteries, and close the case.
assembly.notes: The case is designed for a 1.0 mm thick PCB — match this when ordering your C1 board.
